decisions.quote: We found that the 1973 results were consistently replicated, and the Dr. Fox effect (as defined and measured by the original researchers) stands empirically as a solid effect even after 40 years, despite the old-fashioned movie of the lecture and the shift to a population of college students. However, we also found that the critical flaw of the research was at the level of the conceptual conclusions. Naftulin et al. (1973) interpreted their findings erroneously, thereby misleading generations of researchers and academicians.
decisions.reason: The authors consistently replicated the original positive ratings on the 1973 questionnaire across samples, but their main message is that the original instrument did not validly measure illusory learning because students directly asked about learning reported they had not learned.
